review_items.rationale: Reviewed the fixed v3 plan and harness at direct-checks/5ab07ba90a524b3d84aeeacbcbfe0120 against completed CheckRun 6e663440d82d463f8ed904152fd7db44 (exit 0). The requirement follows from per-request ctx retention and batch_context_expectation, with exact-context lookup in pendingReadIndex.addReady making response identity necessary. Launch and bootstrap create all three voting members and initial entries; updates are appended and State saved before outbound delivery; actual committed configuration entries are applied. Real ticks, votes, no-op replication and NotifyRaftLastApplied establish term 2 and commit/applied 4. The fixture does not overwrite votes, commitment, read pending objects, handlers or quorum state. Peer.ReadIndex permits the supplied distinct nonzero contexts. The only transport fault is loss of two first-context heartbeats, which is permitted by the transport send-failure paths; delivered messages are FIFO. In one synchronous history, prefix event 0 names origin 2 and actual follower readiness, admission event 4 reads its actual pending readStatus context 101/30, and event 14 reads actual GetUpdate.ReadyToReads context 202/30 before Commit clears it. The response at event 13 was produced by the real confirmation handler after actual heartbeat acknowledgments. Identity is scenario plus origin; exactly one operation is issued per origin, and context is only the compared value. The control origin 3 independently associates prefix 1, admission 10 and result 16, retaining 202/30. These match the recorded monitor correlations, with no parse loss or missing results. Term and membership remain stable by the fixed driver and endpoint observations. This establishes the local context-substitution defect; the test process passing is not the basis of the verdict. The v3 oracle compares actual numeric ctx_low and ctx_high rather than formatted strings. Low is 101 at admission event 4 and 202 at result 14, while High is independently 30 at both. For origin 3 both fields match events 10 and 16. Thus ready_context_low_preserved is violated and ready_context_high_preserved holds in this run; the latter does not establish High preservation for unequal input High values. Preserved boundary evidence: Origin 3 retains its admitted context; the bug affects earlier forwarded reads completed under another request context. Local leader read completion uses s.ctx and is not shown defective. Peer sender-membership and message-term guards remain enabled.

items.rationale: Reviewed the fixed v2 plan and harness at direct-checks/c35c44a8b95242108a8c95d2c000f266 against completed CheckRun b74acd29ff6545e8b658b079dc9a48c4 (exit 0). The requirement follows from per-request ctx retention and batch_context_expectation, with exact-context lookup in pendingReadIndex.addReady making response identity necessary. Launch and bootstrap create all three voting members and initial entries; updates are appended and State saved before outbound delivery; actual committed configuration entries are applied. Real ticks, votes, no-op replication and NotifyRaftLastApplied establish term 2 and commit/applied 4. The fixture does not overwrite votes, commitment, read pending objects, handlers or quorum state. Peer.ReadIndex permits the supplied distinct nonzero contexts. The only transport fault is loss of two first-context heartbeats, which is permitted by the transport send-failure paths; delivered messages are FIFO. In one synchronous history, prefix event 0 names origin 2 and actual follower readiness, admission event 4 reads its actual pending readStatus context 101/30, and event 14 reads actual GetUpdate.ReadyToReads context 202/30 before Commit clears it. The response at event 13 was produced by the real confirmation handler after actual heartbeat acknowledgments. Identity is scenario plus origin; exactly one operation is issued per origin, and context is only the compared value. Term and membership remain stable by the fixed driver and endpoint observations. This establishes the local context-substitution defect; the test process passing is not the basis of the verdict. Preserved contrary-scope evidence: Origin 3 retains its admitted context; the bug affects earlier forwarded reads completed under another request context. Local leader read completion uses s.ctx and is not shown defective. Peer sender-membership and message-term guards remain enabled.
